projects.title: Descent | Ascent
projects.intro: An autobiographical p5.js game exploring self-perception and choices

details.description: This zine playfully explores the silent, soggy language of divers. Structured as a journey from descent to ascent, it documents how hand gestures become a form of communication when speech disappears underwater. Inspired by real-world diver signaling systems and research in underwater gesture recognition, the project turns practical survival gestures into an unspoken narrative. It’s part observation, part miscommunication, and entirely an ode to talking with your hands when no one can hear you anyway.

projects.title: Mountain Spirit 山鬼
projects.intro: An retro Futuristic Diner built with MAYA

details.description:
Mountain Spirit is an interactive installation inspired by the Chinese mythological figure Shan Gui and Jeremiah 10:3–5. It reflects on how societies create gods—and meaning itself—through shared imagination, belief, and repetition.

They cut a tree from the forest,
a craftsman shapes it with his hands;
they adorn it with silver and gold,
fasten it with nails and hammers so that it will not move.
It stands upright like a palm tree, but cannot speak;
it must be carried because it cannot walk.

projects.title: Autobiographical Game
projects.intro: An autobiographical p5.js game exploring self-perception and choices

details.description:
An autobiographical p5.js game I did base on my memory with my dog Xiaowu who passed away years before. It depicts my childhood memory imaging my self as a witch and Xiaowu as my familiar spirit. The visual of the game is inspired by Pixel Jeff. The game used p5.play library to create different scenes and interactions. Players can explore the environment, interact with objects, and experience the story through simple gameplay mechanics.
I miss Xiaowu.

projects.title: Experimental Clock
projects.intro: Data visualization

details.description: For this project, I use the number of ripples to present Hour (12-hour timing since this looks prettier), the number of rings per ripple to represent minutes(using 10 minutes as an interval). To avoid the situation that nothing is shown when the minutes is single digit, the point in the middle represent single digits. For example, if there is 3 points when pressing the mouse, That means it is around 3 AM/PM o'clock, if there is 4 ripples and each ripple has 1 point and 2 rings, that means it's about 4:20 (need to minus the single digit ring). Also, if moving the mouse while pressed, you can fast forward the time or rewind it.

projects.title: Ophelia
projects.intro: A plaster-casting sculpture capturing the ethereal buoyancy of a floating body.

details.description:
Idea: A plaster-casting sculpture that captures the ethereal essence of a floating person. Because whole-body casting is difficult, selected body parts (face and hands) are composed to form a harmonious figure, inspired by the image of a swimmer and the paintings of Ophelia. The piece explores the tension between the solid, tactile texture of plaster and a feeling of weightlessness.

My plaster-casting sculpture showcases select parts of the face and hands in detail to convey beauty and mystery in suspension—where heaviness meets float.

projects.title: Bone Clock
projects.intro: A wearble sculpture

details.description: This wearable sculpture turns my anxiety about time into a physical experience. Laser-cut pieces form a mechanical spine worn on the back, which stiffens and shifts as a clock mechanism moves. As time passes, the structure subtly tightens, echoing the way my own back tenses under pressure. The piece makes the invisible weight of time visible—and felt—on the body.

projects.title: Maternity
projects.intro: Watercolor drawings exploring identity as a mother

details.description: This series of paintings was inspired by my mother. During my high school years, she was struggling to balance her roles as a mother, a wife, and a daughter. My grandfather was suffering from depression, and my grandmother was ill. At the same time, I was going through my college application process and needed her support. Witnessing her efforts to hold everything together deeply moved me, and this work reflects her quiet resilience and the weight of familial responsibility.
